blogs.title: TAVI Is a Lifetime Strategy: Planning the Third Valve at the First Implant
blogs.description: This post would use the case to explore the concept of 'lifetime management' in aortic valve disease. It would discuss how expanding TAVI indications and longer patient survival make serial redo procedures increasingly relevant, and why initial choices about valve type, implant depth, commissural alignment and coronary access should be made with future reintervention in mind.

blogs.title: CT Before the Third Valve: Imaging the TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV Patient
blogs.description: This post would focus on preprocedural imaging strategy for complex redo TAVI. It would review the CT features that matter most in layered transcatheter prostheses—coronary ostial height, sinus dimensions, valve-to-coronary distance, anticipated neo-skirt, frame interaction and residual lumen diameter—and show how these measurements can guide valve selection, implant depth and the decision to proceed without coronary protection.

blogs.title: Redo TAVI After Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis: When Is Infection Truly 'Over'?
blogs.description: This post would examine the tension between guideline preference for surgery in prosthetic valve endocarditis and the real-world need to individualize care in prohibitive-risk patients. It would highlight the clinical criteria used to declare infection resolved—completed antibiotics, negative blood cultures, TEE and CT showing no active endocarditis or paravalvular complications—and discuss when prior endocarditis should influence, but not automatically preclude, transcatheter reintervention.

blogs.title: Why Was the Gradient 67 mm Hg Right After TAVI? Interpreting Hemodynamics in Triple-Valve Anatomy
blogs.description: This post would unpack the immediate postprocedural finding of severe residual gradients despite technically successful implantation and no regurgitation. It would review prosthesis-patient mismatch, Doppler pitfalls after redo valve procedures, the effect of constrained frame expansion, and why gradients may improve over time after post-dilation, leaflet stabilization and remodeling of flow through overlapping valve frames.

blogs.title: Choosing the Valve for a Valve-in-Valve-in-Valve: Why Acurate neo2 Made Sense Here
blogs.description: This post would analyze device selection in a narrow, triple-stented aortic root. It would compare self-expanding platforms in the redo setting and explain the rationale for choosing Acurate neo2—supra-annular leaflet position, lower frame profile, favorable hemodynamics and support for commissural alignment—while also addressing the procedural strategy of high implantation to preserve effective orifice area and future coronary access.
